title: The Godfather
description: The Godfather follows the Corleone family, an Italian American crime dynasty balancing private loyalty with public violence. Don Vito Corleone tries to preserve influence through favors, intimidation, and ritualized family power. Michael Corleone begins as an outsider to the family business, but war, assassination attempts, and revenge pull him into the center of the empire. The film is useful for searches about organized crime, succession, family loyalty, political corruption, moral compromise, and the cost of becoming powerful.

title: The Shawshank Redemption
description: The Shawshank Redemption follows Andy Dufresne, a banker wrongly convicted of murdering his wife and her lover. Inside Shawshank Prison, he builds a lasting friendship with Red while quietly resisting a corrupt and dehumanizing institution. The story is less about escape as an action event and more about patience, dignity, literacy, money, memory, and hope over decades. It is strong context for queries about wrongful conviction, prison life, friendship, institutional abuse, long-term planning, and emotional endurance.

title: Pulp Fiction
description: Pulp Fiction weaves together criminals, hitmen, a boxer, a mob boss, and small-time robbers in a nonlinear portrait of Los Angeles crime. The film is known for long conversations, sudden violence, pop culture references, dark comedy, and stories that circle back on themselves. Vincent Vega and Jules Winnfield move through absurd and dangerous situations that often become philosophical without losing their street-level tension. It is useful for semantic searches about nonlinear storytelling, gangster cinema, redemption, chance, violence, and stylized dialogue.

title: Inception
description: Inception follows Dom Cobb, a professional thief who steals secrets by entering dreams. He is hired to do the opposite: implant an idea inside a corporate heir's subconscious so deeply that the target believes it is his own. The film builds a layered heist across dreams within dreams, where architecture, memory, guilt, time dilation, and grief shape the mission. It works well for queries about dream logic, corporate espionage, subconscious manipulation, ambiguous endings, emotional trauma, and science fiction action.

title: Fight Club
description: Fight Club follows an unnamed narrator whose insomnia, consumer exhaustion, and emotional numbness lead him to Tyler Durden. Together they create an underground fight club that begins as physical release and evolves into an anti-consumerist movement with dangerous political consequences. The film examines masculinity, alienation, identity collapse, capitalism, violence, cult behavior, and dissociation. It is especially relevant for searches about unreliable narration, social rebellion, mental health, nihilism, and the split between ordinary life and hidden rage.

title: Forrest Gump
description: Forrest Gump follows a kind-hearted man who moves through several decades of American history without fully understanding his influence on the world around him. Forrest encounters war, protest movements, business success, sports fame, and political moments while remaining emotionally tied to Jenny, his mother, and Lieutenant Dan. The film mixes romance, comedy, melodrama, and historical nostalgia through a character defined by innocence and persistence. It is useful for searches about destiny, American culture, disability, Vietnam, friendship, love, and perseverance.

title: The Matrix
description: The Matrix follows Neo, a hacker who discovers that everyday reality is a simulated world designed by machines to control humanity. Morpheus and Trinity introduce him to a rebellion fighting from outside the illusion, where knowledge becomes both liberation and danger. The film combines cyberpunk design, martial arts, philosophy, artificial intelligence, prophecy, and questions about free will. It is strong context for queries about simulation theory, virtual reality, machine control, awakening, chosen-one narratives, and resistance against systems.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
description: The Fellowship of the Ring begins Frodo Baggins's journey after he inherits the One Ring, an object tied to the dark lord Sauron. A fellowship of hobbits, humans, an elf, a dwarf, and a wizard forms to carry the ring toward destruction before it corrupts Middle-earth. The film introduces epic fantasy through friendship, temptation, ancient evil, sacrifice, and the burden placed on ordinary people. It is useful for searches about magical rings, heroic quests, fellowship, elves, hobbits, wizards, and fantasy worldbuilding.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
description: The Two Towers follows the fractured heroes after the Fellowship breaks apart. Frodo and Sam continue toward Mordor with the unstable guidance of Gollum, while Aragorn, Legolas, and Gimli become involved in the defense of Rohan. The Battle of Helm's Deep provides a major portrait of military desperation, courage, and alliance under overwhelming threat. The film is useful for searches about divided quests, war strategy, corrupted guides, loyalty, siege battles, Saruman, and the growth of hope during crisis.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
description: The Return of the King concludes the war for Middle-earth by combining intimate sacrifice with enormous battlefield stakes. Frodo and Sam approach Mount Doom as the Ring becomes heavier psychologically and physically, while Aragorn accepts the responsibilities of kingship. The film explores courage, temptation, mercy, friendship, political restoration, and the emotional aftermath of victory. It is strong context for queries about epic endings, final battles, heroic sacrifice, kingship, Mordor, and the destruction of a corrupting artifact.

title: The Dark Knight
description: The Dark Knight places Batman against the Joker, a criminal who treats chaos as a weapon and morality as a social experiment. Gotham City becomes a testing ground for fear, surveillance, justice, public trust, and the limits of heroic restraint. Harvey Dent's fall from idealistic prosecutor to vengeful figure shows how symbols can be corrupted under pressure. The film is useful for searches about superhero crime drama, anarchy, urban terrorism, moral dilemmas, vigilantism, sacrifice, and psychological villains.

title: Schindler's List
description: Schindler's List dramatizes Oskar Schindler's transformation from opportunistic businessman to rescuer of Jewish workers during the Holocaust. The film shows how bureaucracy, profit, terror, and personal courage intersect under Nazi occupation. Its emotional force comes from the contrast between industrialized cruelty and individual acts of protection. It is important context for searches about World War II, genocide, Holocaust memory, moral responsibility, survival, industrial labor, and the difference one compromised person can still make.

title: Goodfellas
description: Goodfellas follows Henry Hill's rise inside the Italian American mob and his eventual collapse under paranoia, drugs, betrayal, and law enforcement pressure. The film presents organized crime as seductive, funny, violent, and exhausting rather than glamorous in a simple way. It focuses on everyday rituals of gangsters, loyalty codes, money, restaurants, status, and sudden brutality. It is useful for searches about mafia life, crime biography, New York gangsters, informants, cocaine, betrayal, and criminal decline.

title: Interstellar
description: Interstellar follows astronauts who travel through a wormhole to search for a habitable planet as Earth faces ecological collapse. Cooper leaves his daughter Murph behind, and their relationship becomes central to the film's treatment of time, gravity, love, and sacrifice. The story blends hard science concepts with emotional melodrama, including relativity, black holes, dust storms, and survival of the species. It is strong context for searches about space exploration, wormholes, time dilation, parent-child bonds, climate crisis, and humanity's future.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
description: The Silence of the Lambs follows Clarice Starling, an FBI trainee investigating a serial killer while consulting the imprisoned psychiatrist Hannibal Lecter. Clarice's intelligence, vulnerability, and trauma become part of a psychological duel with Lecter, who offers insight while manipulating every conversation. The film mixes procedural investigation, horror, behavioral profiling, gender pressure, and intimate menace. It is useful for searches about serial killers, FBI profiling, cannibal villains, psychological suspense, trauma, and the relationship between investigator and monster.

title: The Green Mile
description: The Green Mile is set on death row, where prison guard Paul Edgecomb meets John Coffey, a condemned man with mysterious healing powers. The story combines supernatural elements with prison drama, moral doubt, racism, cruelty, and compassion. John Coffey's innocence and suffering force the guards to question punishment, justice, and mercy. It is useful for searches about death penalty, miracles, wrongful execution, empathy, spiritual healing, institutional violence, and emotionally heavy drama.

title: Gladiator
description: Gladiator follows Maximus, a respected Roman general betrayed by Commodus after the death of Emperor Marcus Aurelius. Reduced to slavery, Maximus becomes a gladiator whose skill in the arena turns him into a symbol against imperial corruption. The film combines revenge, political legitimacy, spectacle, grief, and the longing to reunite with family after death. It works well for searches about ancient Rome, gladiatorial combat, betrayal, tyranny, honor, revenge, and heroic tragedy.

title: The Lion King
description: The Lion King follows Simba, a young lion prince who flees after the death of his father Mufasa. Scar manipulates Simba's guilt and seizes power, turning the Pride Lands into a broken kingdom. Simba's return becomes a story about grief, identity, responsibility, ancestry, and the cycle of life. The film is useful for searches about Disney animation, royal succession, animal kingdom drama, family loss, coming of age, and reclaiming a rightful place.

title: Back to the Future
description: Back to the Future follows Marty McFly, a teenager who accidentally travels from 1985 to 1955 in a DeLorean time machine built by Doc Brown. In the past, Marty disrupts his parents' first meeting and risks erasing his own existence. The film turns time travel into a fast, comedic adventure about family history, teenage identity, causality, music, and invention. It is useful for searches about time loops, paradoxes, 1950s culture, science comedy, modified cars, and changing the past.

title: City of God
description: City of God portrays the growth of organized crime in a Rio de Janeiro favela across several decades. Buscape tries to escape violence through photography, while other children are pulled into drug trafficking, weapons, status, and revenge. The film shows how poverty, policing, ambition, and childhood exposure to brutality shape different futures. It is strong context for searches about Brazilian cinema, favela life, urban crime, photography, social inequality, youth violence, and survival in marginalized communities.

title: Parasite
description: Parasite follows the poor Kim family as they gradually infiltrate the household of the wealthy Park family through deception and performance. What begins as social satire becomes a tense thriller about class dependence, resentment, architecture, smell, weather, and hidden spaces. The house itself becomes a map of inequality, with upstairs luxury and buried desperation below. It is useful for searches about class conflict, black comedy, Korean cinema, social mobility, domestic labor, and violent reversals.

title: Amelie
description: Amelie follows a shy young woman in Paris who decides to improve the lives of strangers through small secret interventions. Her imagination transforms ordinary apartments, cafes, train stations, and photo booths into a playful emotional puzzle. While helping others reconnect, she must confront her own loneliness and fear of intimacy. The film is strong context for searches about whimsical romance, Paris, kindness, magical realism, introversion, color-rich visual style, and gentle emotional transformation.

title: The Usual Suspects
description: The Usual Suspects revolves around Verbal Kint's account of how a group of criminals became involved with the terrifying figure Keyser Soze. The film uses interrogation, flashbacks, unreliable narration, and criminal mythology to keep the truth unstable. Its central pleasure is the way details are rearranged by the final revelation. It is useful for searches about crime mystery, twist endings, deceptive storytelling, police questioning, hidden identity, and legendary villains.

title: Se7en
description: Se7en follows two detectives investigating murders staged around the seven deadly sins. Somerset's weary intelligence contrasts with Mills's impatience as they move through a grim, rain-soaked city defined by moral decay. The killer uses each crime as a message about guilt, sin, punishment, and social rot. The film is strong context for searches about serial killer thrillers, religious symbolism, detective partnerships, urban darkness, psychological horror, and devastating endings.

title: Saving Private Ryan
description: Saving Private Ryan opens with the brutal D-Day landing at Omaha Beach and then follows soldiers sent to find one surviving paratrooper. The mission raises painful questions about whether one life is worth risking many others. Captain Miller's squad encounters fear, duty, resentment, sacrifice, and the randomness of combat. It is useful for searches about World War II, Normandy, battlefield realism, rescue missions, military ethics, trauma, and brotherhood among soldiers.

title: Joker
description: Joker follows Arthur Fleck, an isolated clown and failed comedian living in a decaying Gotham City. Social neglect, mental illness, humiliation, poverty, and media spectacle push him toward a violent persona that others begin to mythologize. The film treats villain origin as a mix of personal breakdown and public unrest. It is useful for searches about comic book villains, psychological collapse, social alienation, Gotham, class resentment, unreliable perception, and dark character studies.

title: The Truman Show
description: The Truman Show follows Truman Burbank, a man whose entire life has unknowingly been staged and broadcast as television entertainment. Small glitches in his controlled town reveal that his marriage, friendships, job, and environment are manufactured. The story becomes a satire of media, surveillance, advertising, reality television, and the human need for authentic choice. It is useful for searches about artificial reality, hidden cameras, free will, manipulation, celebrity culture, and escaping a designed world.

title: Whiplash
description: Whiplash follows Andrew Neiman, an ambitious jazz drummer trying to become one of the greats. His teacher Fletcher uses intimidation, humiliation, and psychological abuse while claiming that greatness requires extreme pressure. The film turns rehearsal rooms and competitions into battlefields of ego, discipline, fear, and obsession. It is useful for searches about jazz, drumming, perfectionism, abusive mentorship, artistic ambition, music conservatories, and the cost of excellence.

title: Spirited Away
description: Spirited Away follows Chihiro, a young girl trapped in a spirit world after her parents are transformed into pigs. She must work in a bathhouse ruled by a powerful witch while learning courage, discipline, memory, and compassion. The film blends Japanese folklore, environmental themes, labor, identity loss, and dreamlike visual imagination. It is strong context for searches about Studio Ghibli, spirits, coming of age, magic bathhouses, childhood fear, and transformation.

title: The Shining
description: The Shining follows Jack Torrance, a struggling writer who becomes winter caretaker of the isolated Overlook Hotel. The building's violent past, supernatural presence, and Jack's own resentment merge into a threat against his wife Wendy and son Danny. The film creates horror through space, repetition, family tension, addiction, psychic visions, and claustrophobic isolation. It is useful for searches about haunted hotels, psychological horror, cabin fever, domestic violence, writers, and iconic horror imagery.

title: Django Unchained
description: Django Unchained follows Django, an enslaved man freed by the German bounty hunter Dr. King Schultz. Django learns the bounty trade while searching for his wife Broomhilda, who is held on a brutal plantation. The film mixes western revenge, slavery, dark comedy, stylized violence, and racial power dynamics. It is useful for searches about bounty hunters, plantations, rescue missions, revenge westerns, slavery in America, and Tarantino dialogue.

title: Inglourious Basterds
description: Inglourious Basterds reimagines World War II through intersecting plots to destroy Nazi leadership inside a French cinema. The story follows Jewish American soldiers, the vengeful theater owner Shosanna, and the terrifyingly polite officer Hans Landa. Language, performance, accents, cinema, and identity become tools of survival and violence. It is useful for searches about alternate history, Nazis, resistance, espionage, revenge, undercover tension, and film as a weapon.

title: The Big Lebowski
description: The Big Lebowski follows Jeff Lebowski, known as the Dude, after he is mistaken for a wealthy man with the same name. A ruined rug, a kidnapping scheme, bowling friends, nihilists, artists, and criminals pull him into a mystery he barely wants to solve. The comedy comes from his relaxed personality colliding with increasingly absurd noir situations. It is useful for searches about cult comedy, mistaken identity, bowling, Los Angeles weirdness, ransom plots, and laid-back antiheroes.

title: Reservoir Dogs
description: Reservoir Dogs follows a group of criminals after a diamond heist collapses into bloodshed and suspicion. The surviving thieves gather in a warehouse and begin to suspect that one of them is an undercover police officer. The film uses fragmented chronology, tense dialogue, violence, pop music, and shifting loyalties. It is useful for searches about failed robberies, criminal paranoia, undercover cops, betrayal, warehouse standoffs, and independent crime cinema.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
description: 2001: A Space Odyssey traces human evolution from prehistoric apes to a mysterious mission near Jupiter. Monoliths appear at key moments, suggesting contact with an intelligence beyond human understanding. Aboard the spacecraft, the computer HAL 9000 shifts from calm assistant to deadly obstacle, raising questions about machine consciousness and control. The film is useful for searches about philosophical science fiction, artificial intelligence, space travel, evolution, cosmic mystery, and visual storytelling.

title: Taxi Driver
description: Taxi Driver follows Travis Bickle, a lonely Vietnam veteran driving a cab through nighttime New York. He grows disgusted by the city's violence, sex work, politics, and perceived moral decay while becoming increasingly unstable. His desire to cleanse the world turns into a violent fantasy of purpose. The film is useful for searches about urban alienation, antiheroes, mental instability, vigilantism, loneliness, postwar trauma, and 1970s New York.

title: Apocalypse Now
description: Apocalypse Now follows Captain Willard on a secret mission during the Vietnam War to assassinate Colonel Kurtz. Traveling upriver into the jungle, Willard encounters surreal violence, military absurdity, colonial echoes, and psychological breakdown. Kurtz becomes both target and mirror, representing the war's moral collapse. The film is useful for searches about Vietnam, jungle warfare, madness, imperialism, river journeys, military horror, and the darkness of power.

title: Citizen Kane
description: Citizen Kane investigates the life of Charles Foster Kane after his final word, Rosebud, becomes a journalistic mystery. Through interviews and fragmented memories, the film reconstructs Kane's rise as a newspaper magnate, political figure, collector, and lonely man. Its structure explores how wealth and public influence fail to recover private loss. It is useful for searches about media power, memory, ambition, childhood trauma, nonlinear biography, and cinematic innovation.

title: Pan's Labyrinth
description: Pan's Labyrinth follows Ofelia, a young girl in post-Civil War Spain living under the authority of a brutal fascist stepfather. She discovers a dark fairy-tale world that offers tasks, monsters, and the possibility of a hidden identity. The film contrasts political violence with fantasy, showing imagination as both refuge and moral test. It is useful for searches about dark fantasy, fascism, childhood, Spanish history, fauns, resistance, and sacrifice.

title: Memento
description: Memento follows Leonard Shelby, a man unable to form new memories after a traumatic attack. He investigates his wife's murder using Polaroid photos, tattoos, handwritten notes, and routines that may be manipulated by others. The reverse structure forces the viewer to experience confusion, suspicion, and dependency on incomplete evidence. It is useful for searches about memory loss, revenge, unreliable perception, nonlinear editing, tattoos, investigation, and self-deception.

title: Die Hard
description: Die Hard follows John McClane, a New York police officer trapped inside a Los Angeles skyscraper during a Christmas party. Terrorists led by Hans Gruber take hostages, including McClane's estranged wife, while hiding a sophisticated robbery plan. McClane survives through improvisation, pain, humor, and knowledge of the building. It is useful for searches about action thrillers, hostage situations, Christmas movies, skyscrapers, lone cops, heists, and practical heroism.

title: Terminator 2: Judgment Day
description: Terminator 2: Judgment Day follows Sarah Connor and her son John, the future leader of human resistance against machines. A reprogrammed Terminator protects John from the T-1000, a liquid-metal assassin sent from the future. The film combines chase action, family bonds, nuclear anxiety, artificial intelligence, and the possibility of changing fate. It is useful for searches about time travel, killer robots, Skynet, apocalypse, protective machines, and destiny versus choice.

title: Alien
description: Alien follows the crew of the commercial starship Nostromo after they answer a mysterious signal on a remote planet. A hostile organism enters the ship, grows through terrifying life stages, and hunts the crew in confined industrial corridors. Ripley emerges as a rational survivor while corporate priorities and biological horror intensify the threat. The film is useful for searches about space horror, xenomorphs, alien creatures, isolation, survival, body horror, and science fiction suspense.

title: Blade Runner
description: Blade Runner follows Rick Deckard, a specialist assigned to hunt escaped replicants in a rain-soaked future Los Angeles. The replicants seek longer lives and meaning, which complicates the line between human emotion and artificial existence. The film explores memory, empathy, identity, corporate power, urban decay, and noir atmosphere. It is useful for searches about cyberpunk, androids, artificial intelligence, dystopian cities, implanted memories, and philosophical science fiction.

title: Psycho
description: Psycho follows Marion Crane after she steals money and stops at the isolated Bates Motel. Norman Bates appears shy and polite, but his relationship with his mother hides a violent psychological secret. The film transforms a crime story into horror through voyeurism, guilt, identity fracture, and sudden narrative disruption. It is useful for searches about Hitchcock, motel horror, shower scene, split personality, suspense, murder, and classic psychological thrillers.

title: Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope
description: Star Wars: A New Hope follows Luke Skywalker as he leaves his desert home and joins the Rebel Alliance against the Galactic Empire. With Leia, Han Solo, Obi-Wan Kenobi, and two droids, he learns about the Force and confronts the Death Star. The film blends space opera, mythic adventure, political rebellion, fantasy, and swashbuckling action. It is useful for searches about Jedi, Darth Vader, lightsabers, rebellion, space battles, and hero's journey stories.

title: Star Wars: Episode V - The Empire Strikes Back
description: The Empire Strikes Back deepens the conflict between the Rebel Alliance and the Empire after the destruction of the Death Star. Luke trains with Yoda while Han, Leia, Chewbacca, and C-3PO flee imperial pursuit. Darth Vader becomes more personal and terrifying, leading to one of the most famous family revelations in film. It is useful for searches about Jedi training, Hoth, Cloud City, the dark side, tragic twists, and middle chapters.

title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
description: Raiders of the Lost Ark follows Indiana Jones, an archaeologist and adventurer racing Nazis to find the Ark of the Covenant. The film combines ancient traps, religious artifacts, desert expeditions, fistfights, humor, and romance with Marion Ravenwood. Indiana is both scholar and action hero, using knowledge and improvisation under pressure. It is useful for searches about archaeology adventures, lost relics, Nazi villains, treasure hunts, biblical artifacts, and serial-style action.

title: Jurassic Park
description: Jurassic Park imagines a theme park where scientists have recreated dinosaurs through genetic engineering. Visitors experience wonder before security failures turn the park into a survival nightmare. The story questions commercial ambition, scientific responsibility, chaos theory, and humanity's illusion of control over nature. It is useful for searches about dinosaurs, DNA, theme parks, velociraptors, Tyrannosaurus rex, science ethics, and creature suspense.

title: Titanic
description: Titanic combines a fictional romance with the historical sinking of the RMS Titanic. Jack, a poor artist, and Rose, a wealthy young woman trapped by class expectations, fall in love during the ship's maiden voyage. The disaster turns social hierarchy, courage, cowardice, memory, and survival into a large-scale melodrama. It is useful for searches about shipwrecks, iceberg disasters, forbidden romance, class divisions, historical tragedy, and epic cinema.

title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
description: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial follows Elliott, a lonely boy who befriends an alien stranded on Earth. Elliott and his siblings hide the creature from adults and government agents while trying to help him contact home. The film treats alien contact as a story of childhood empathy, wonder, fear, and farewell rather than invasion. It is useful for searches about friendly aliens, children, bicycles, suburban science fiction, telepathic bonds, and going home.

title: Jaws
description: Jaws follows a seaside town threatened by a great white shark during the tourist season. Police chief Brody wants to close the beaches, but local economic pressure keeps people in danger. The final hunt brings Brody, marine biologist Hooper, and shark hunter Quint onto the open water. It is useful for searches about shark attacks, beach towns, suspense, invisible threats, summer tourism, ocean fear, and survival at sea.

title: The Sixth Sense
description: The Sixth Sense follows Cole, a frightened boy who says he can see dead people, and Malcolm Crowe, the child psychologist trying to help him. The story blends ghost horror with emotional drama about listening, grief, fear, and unresolved pain. Cole's encounters with the dead become less like random scares and more like requests for help. It is useful for searches about ghosts, child trauma, twist endings, psychologists, supernatural mystery, and grief.

title: A Beautiful Mind
description: A Beautiful Mind dramatizes the life of mathematician John Nash, whose brilliance is complicated by schizophrenia and paranoid delusions. The film follows his academic work, marriage to Alicia, struggles with perception, and eventual recognition. It turns abstract mathematical achievement into a story about love, illness, discipline, and survival with a fragile mind. It is useful for searches about mathematics, Nobel Prize, mental illness, hallucinations, academia, and personal resilience.

title: Scent of a Woman
description: Scent of a Woman follows Charlie, a student hired to accompany Frank Slade, a blind retired officer with a sharp tongue and self-destructive streak. Their trip to New York becomes a confrontation with pleasure, despair, honor, and moral courage. Frank challenges Charlie's fear while Charlie gives Frank a reason to keep living. It is useful for searches about blindness, mentorship, tango scenes, integrity, school discipline, and unlikely friendship.

title: American Beauty
description: American Beauty follows Lester Burnham, a middle-aged suburban man in a crisis of marriage, work, desire, and identity. His rebellion against routine exposes the emptiness and repression inside his family and neighborhood. The film satirizes consumer comfort while moving toward violence, longing, voyeurism, and fragile beauty. It is useful for searches about suburban dysfunction, midlife crisis, appearances, alienation, family secrets, and American social satire.

title: Collateral Beauty
description: Collateral Beauty follows Howard, an advertising executive devastated by personal loss and unable to reconnect with work or friends. His grief is explored through encounters with figures representing Love, Time, and Death, whether literal, staged, or emotionally symbolic. The film uses melodrama and allegory to examine mourning, friendship, responsibility, and the search for meaning after tragedy. It is useful for searches about grief, loss, emotional healing, abstract concepts, friendship interventions, and life after trauma.

title: The Pursuit of Happyness
description: The Pursuit of Happyness follows Chris Gardner as he struggles with homelessness, unpaid work, single fatherhood, and financial instability. The film emphasizes perseverance, dignity, ambition, exhaustion, and the emotional burden of economic survival. It is useful for searches about poverty, father-son relationships, homelessness, career ambition, sales, internships, and inspirational drama.

title: Cast Away
description: Cast Away follows Chuck Noland, a time-obsessed executive stranded alone on a deserted island after a plane crash. title: Gravity
description: Gravity follows astronaut Ryan Stone after debris destroys her shuttle mission and leaves her drifting in orbit. The film turns space into a hostile environment of silence, motion, beauty, and danger. It is useful for searches about astronauts, orbital disasters, survival in space, isolation, oxygen, debris fields, and rebirth imagery.

title: Mad Max: Fury Road

The film uses practical action, chase structure, visual intensity, and minimal dialogue to tell a liberation story. It is useful for searches about desert action, car chases, post-apocalypse, feminism, survival, war rigs, and rebellion.

title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind

title: Groundhog Day

title: Central Station

title: Elite Squad

title: A Dog's Will

title: The Second Mother

title: Bacurau

title: I'm Still Here

title: Inside Out

title: Toy Story
description: Toy Story imagines toys that come alive when humans are not watching.
